raw.retained_raw_text: {"schema_version":"chat_response_v1","response_type":"answer","answer_text":"The light-dependent reactions convert light energy into chemical energy stored in energy carriers, which the Calvin cycle then uses. Their overall purpose is to convert light energy into chemical energy that the Calvin cycle uses to fuel the assembly of sugar molecules [ev_008]. Photosystems absorb light and use electron transport chains to convert energy into the chemical energy of ATP and NADPH [ev_002]. These energy carriers travel into the stroma, where the Calvin cycle reactions take place [ev_007]. The carriers that move energy from the light-dependent reactions to the Calvin cycle can be thought of as \"full\" because they bring energy; after the energy is released, the \"empty\" carriers return to the light-dependent reactions to obtain more energy [ev_001].
